name: Beefeater
label: Dischord
lede: Two years, two LPs, a vegetarian singer fronting a band called Beefeater, and a guitarist who taught DC punk to swing.

eras.title: A Swiss kid, a slap bass, a vegetarian's band
eras.text: Tomas Squip came to Washington from Switzerland around 1981 and drummed in Red C before he ever sang. By 1984 he had a band built on Fred Smith's guitar and Dug Birdzell's bass, and a sound that took as much from funk and jazz as from hardcore.

years.h: Squip arrives, and drums for Red C
years.p: About nineteen and new to DC from Switzerland, [[Tomas Squip|273702be-180d-487a-9238-2154aea60b92]] plays drums in Red C. He'd go vegetarian within a year or so, a choice that ended up coloring the whole scene.
Squip sings. Fred "Freak" Smith, a Howard University music-education student whose father sang doo-wop, plays guitar. Dug E. Bird plays bass, Bruce Atchley Taylor drums.
Beefeater debut at Food for Thought, the DC restaurant that hosted punk shows. Funk, thrash and reggae in one set, with Squip's lyrics about politics and spirit.
years.xp:
Dischord's history dates the first show to the summer of 1984 and the band's active run to fall 1984 through fall 1986. The mix was the point: Smith's guitar was aggressive but loose, and Birdzell slapped his bass the way Smith had shown him.

Birdzell has credited Smith with teaching him slap bass. Listeners have heard the [[Minutemen|d4ad0149-d8ae-4105-8009-0221fce9ff35]] in that combination: punk energy pushed through funk and jazz.

eras.title: Revolution Summer
eras.text: DC hardcore had burned out on violence and the kids who came for it. In 1985 a set of bands tried to make it mean something again, and Beefeater, with its politics and its groove, was one of the pillars.

years.h: One of the Revolution Summer bands
years.p: Beefeater play the season alongside [[Embrace|9d1ad8e3-8740-429a-bdc5-52f96a9c4431]], [[Gray Matter|c9065214-ba09-4c2c-b341-35713b702264]] and [[Rites of Spring|b2ff1a6d-9198-4646-b068-8965242d245b]]. Squip's lyrics are political and openly spiritual, unusual on Dischord.

q: The band that made it all right to talk about vegetarianism.
years.p: Recorded at Inner Ear, produced by "Gumbo MacKaye." A Dog Day takes the listener into a slaughterhouse. [[Ian MacKaye|c12f644b-1066-4ead-b0dd-d0c380f5cca2]] was still calling it a great song in 2023.
years.xp:
Squip's vegetarianism wasn't a side note. Soulside's Bobby Sullivan later credited him as the one who got his friends looking at the bigger picture, vegan diet included.

Squip put it simply looking back in 2010: Beefeater gave the scene permission to talk about it.

eras.title: Need a job, then the house burns down
eras.text: Beefeater went through three drummers, put out an EP on another label, and broke up in the fall of 1986 with a finished album nobody had heard yet. Their roadie was about to be in Fugazi.

years.p: The founding drummer leaves. Shellhaas plays on the next release.

years.h: Need a Job EP · Olive Tree Records
years.p: Six songs on Olive Tree, the only Beefeater record not on Dischord.
The third drummer in two years. Craun is behind the kit on the last album.

years.h: The roadie who became a Fugazi
years.p: [[Joe Lally|62046ffd-7d76-476b-bee5-b281b7575c6c]] hauls gear for Beefeater, and through the band meets MacKaye, who Squip was living with. By late summer 1986 Lally is practicing with MacKaye in what becomes [[Fugazi|233fc3f3-6de2-465c-985e-e721dbabbace]].
About two years after the first show, the band is done. The album they'd already made is still unreleased.
Out after the breakup. Squip, Smith, Bird and Craun at Inner Ear, with MacKaye producing again and world music threaded through the funk.

eras.title: Fidelity Jones and Strange Boutique
eras.text: The members scattered into other DC bands, Squip wrote down what he believed for Dischord's own book, and the label put both albums on a single CD.

years.p: The singer and bassist carry on together until spring 1990. Smith joins the goth-leaning [[Strange Boutique|0ee0668b-fa1d-4db1-ac8c-43a3ad1272c0]], Craun the Rhythm Pigs.
His piece lays out a plainly religious worldview, rare among Dischord voices. He later changed his name, first to Onam Ben-Israel and then to Onam Emmet.

years.h: Both albums on one disc · Dischord No. 64
years.p: The whole Dischord run plus bonus tracks, in one place.

eras.title: Freak
eras.text: Fred Smith kept playing long after Beefeater, in bands from post-punk to what he called ghetto metal, and eventually took FREAK as his legal name. His death in 2017 brought the DC scene back to what he'd given it.

years.h: One last DC show at the Black Cat
years.p: Smith's final performance in Washington. By then he'd played in Strange Boutique, American Corpse Flower and Blaxmyth.

q: His guitar playing was such a strong element.
years.h: Fred Smith dies in Los Angeles
years.p: Smith, in his mid-fifties, is found dead in a park in Los Angeles' San Fernando Valley. The death is investigated as a homicide.
years.xp:
MacKaye called his guitar playing a huge part of what Beefeater was. Birdzell credited him with the band's funk, down to teaching him how to slap.

In December 2017 Los Angeles County offered a $10,000 reward for information. Supervisor Sheila Kuehl said Smith paved the way for Black musicians in punk. NPR reported that no one had been named.
